title: The Raven and the Snake
logline: A raven whose chicks are taken again and again by a black snake wants to fight her, but his friend the jackal shows him a cleverer way: steal a necklace in plain sight and let the angry villagers find the snake for him.
moral: Strength is not always the answer; a good plan can defeat an enemy you could never beat by force.
tone: Starts tender and sad, turns sly and playful at the plan, becomes a comic chase, a short sharp scare at the burrow, then a warm, quiet ending. Danger is real but never graphic: both killings happen out of sight (a cut to the sky, a dust cloud).

beats.summary: A raven has a nest high in a tall tree; a dark burrow sits at the foot of it.
Every time the chicks hatch, the black snake comes out of its burrow.
The snake climbs to the nest; the taking happens off screen (down floats past the returning father).
The raven finds the nest empty and grieves, helpless.
His friend the jackal finds him alone and asks what is wrong.
The raven plans revenge by force: peck the sleeping snake in the eyes.
The jackal stops him: the snake is fast and dangerous; strength is not always the answer.
The jackal has a plan; the raven comes close to listen.
The plan as a picture: steal a necklace in public, fly slowly, drop it at the snake burrow.
Morning at the river: a gold necklace glitters on a rock beside a washerwoman.
The raven swoops and takes the necklace in his beak.
The woman cries out and the villagers chase; the raven stays low and waits for them, tree to tree.
He drops the necklace at the mouth of the burrow.
The villagers reach for it and the black snake rises out of the burrow.
They kill the snake (inside a comic fight cloud), take the necklace and go home.
The raven keeps watch for two days: the snake never returns.
The nest fills with new chicks and their voices fill the branches: wit beat strength.

cast.name: the raven
cast.look: Black crow figure exactly as in the catalogue; new optional carry field so the necklace hangs from the beak. Acting through crest, sag, headRot, beak, drop, tailDrop, fly/flap plus gaze, lid, wet, sq, tip.

cast.name: the jackal (ibn awa)
cast.base: fox with a new optional palette (pal:'jackal')
cast.look: Fox drawing recoloured: sandy tan body, grey-black saddle on the back, cream chest and muzzle, black tail tip, slightly taller ears. Calm, clever, half-lidded; older friend.

cast.name: the black snake
cast.look: Fat black tube body with a thin yellow belly line and red Ben-Day dots on the shaded side, wedge head, one large eye2 eye with a yellow iris, forked red tongue. Body follows a path; no legs, so all acting is head, tongue, eye and how the body pours.

cast.name: the washerwoman
cast.look: Wife figure with a blue headscarf instead of the bun, red dress with yellow hem, sleeves rolled. Kneels to wash (new kneel field).

cast.name: villager with the stick
cast.look: Owner figure without the nightcap: white turban, short black beard, blue tunic, carries a staff. Tall, bold, first to arrive.

cast.name: the puffing villager
cast.look: Same villager drawing: red cap, moustache, yellow tunic, 8 % wider and 6 % shorter. Always two steps behind and out of breath.

sets.description: Home set, world 1000 x 1230, ground y 900. sky(day) + hillTrees + ground; one tall tree (Library tree() with custom opts): trunk x 560, crown from y 150 to 470; nest fork at (500, 345); bare low branch pointing left, tip at (430, 690); lookout twig at (600, 215); a root stone at (395, 862). The burrow (prop) is at (860, 890) on the right. Jackal mark x 200. Villagers enter from the left.

The jackal plan as a picture: a large paper-coloured thought cloud (x 60..940, y 90..820) over the dimmed home set, with the jackal head bottom left and the raven bottom right. Inside, a left-to-right strip map: hut and two small people at the left, three small trees, the burrow at the right; step chips 1, 2, 3.

Library river set as in the catalogue (sky preset 'dawn' warming to day, river back/front, riverBank, islandHut on the right bank as the village house, figTree on the left bank). Added: a flat wash rock at about (860, 815) on the right bank and a wet cloth at the water edge near x 700. Check the right-bank ground height in Library/sets before placing.

A 3000-unit-wide strip for the chase: sky(day), hillTrees repeated, ground, and four separate perch trees (Library tree(), small crowns, a clear branch at y 520-560) at x 600, 1250, 1900, 2550; the tall home tree is visible at the far right end. Camera tracks right.

props.description: Library nest: eggs 3, chicks 3 with the ck acting array (gx, gy, wide, open, cw); empty state = eggs 0, chicks 0 plus three shell halves drawn by the scene.
Gold necklace: 9 yellow beads on a black-outlined arc with one red drop gem; hangs and swings from a point; four-point white sparkle that pulses.

Snake hole: a low tan mound (150 x 60) with three grey rocks and a navy oval opening (70 x 46). Drawn in two layers (back, front lip) so the snake comes out between them. States: plain, eyes glinting inside, cobweb + flower (abandoned).
The villager's staff: a brown tapered line 150 units long held in the hand point.
A white cloth with blue dots (a rounded rectangle that folds in two) and a few suds circles.
Library worm, carried in the beak for the chicks.

scenes.summary: Home. The necklace falls at the mouth of the burrow. The villagers run in, a hand reaches for the gold, and the black snake rises behind it.

camera.notes: Base of the tree {x 640, y 760, zoom 1.4}; push to the burrow {x 820, y 830, zoom 2.0} for the drop; at 127.6 back out to {x 600, y 780, zoom 1.3} for the arrival; from 130.4 slow push on hand, necklace and snake {x 790, y 800, zoom 1.9}.

actions.action: arrow and label mark the spot; the raven flies up to the low branch to watch

actions.acting: she is disturbed and curious; raven lid snaps wide

actions.action: second, skirt in one fist, pointing ahead at the glitter
actions.acting: stagger 0.4 s; pointFwd

actions.action: bends and reaches for the necklace
actions.acting: eyes on the gold only; hand closes to within a few units

actions.action: the black head rises out of the hole right behind the necklace, level with his hand
actions.acting: slow rise, 0.4 s; tongue flick at the top

scenes.summary: The fight is a comic dust cloud. When it clears the snake lies still, the woman has her necklace, and the villagers walk home carrying the snake away on the staff.

camera.notes: Wide {x 620, y 780, zoom 1.3}; panel-only shake (4 px, 3 hits) while the cloud is up; from 137.6 pan left a little with the leaving villagers, then stop and let them walk out.

scenes.composition: Cloud centred on the burrow (x 800, y 820, radius about 170), never touching the raven on his branch top left. After it clears: snake limp on the ground left of the burrow, woman centre, men either side.

actions.action: raises the staff high and steps in; man2 winds up behind him
actions.acting: big anticipation: staff back over the shoulder, weight on the back foot

actions.action: a round fight cloud covers the burrow: puffs, stars, the staff tip and the snake tail popping out in turn
actions.acting: no blow is seen; three beats of shake; the woman hops from foot to foot at the edge
actions.library: fightCloud (new effect) from dustBurst + stars; panel-only shake

actions.action: on his branch, throws a wing over his eyes, then peeks through the feathers
actions.acting: sag as a shield, one eye visible (lid 0.6 to 0)

actions.acting: no movement at all; a last puff of dust drifts off

actions.action: steps forward and picks the necklace out of the dust
actions.acting: careful two-finger lift, blows the dust off

actions.action: holds it to her chest and smiles; one sparkle
actions.acting: eyes closed in relief, shoulders drop

actions.action: hooks the limp snake over the end of his staff and shoulders it
actions.acting: held at arm length; man2 mops his brow with his cap

actions.action: the three walk off to the left, man2 last, looking back once at the hole

scenes.summary: The vigil. From the top of the tree the raven watches the burrow while two days and nights wheel past. A cobweb closes the hole and a flower grows beside it: she is not coming back.

camera.notes: Close on the raven at the lookout twig {x 600, y 240, zoom 2.4}; at 142.6 crane back to the whole tree {x 600, y 600, zoom 1.02} and hold through the day cycles; at 148.7 push down to the burrow {x 840, y 850, zoom 2.3}; at 149.9 cut back to the raven close.

scenes.composition: Whole-tree frame: raven tiny at the top, burrow at the bottom right, a dashed eye-line joining them. The sky does the moving.

actions.action: perched at the very top, staring down, not daring to believe it
actions.acting: body still, pupils make small scans of the ground; crest half

actions.action: crane back to show the raven at the top and the burrow at the bottom
actions.acting: a dashed eye-line draws from him down to the hole

actions.action: shifts his feet and settles in to wait
actions.acting: small side-step, feathers fluff, sq 0.95

actions.action: the sun slides down, the sky goes dusk then night with a moon, then dawn
actions.acting: one full cycle in 1.4 s; the raven silhouette stays, his lids droop at night and snap open
actions.library: dayCycle (new): sky presets cross-faded, sun and moon on arcs

actions.action: counter 'DAY 1'
actions.acting: pops with the returning sun

actions.action: second cycle: sun down, moon over, sun up
actions.acting: during the night a spider thread appears across the burrow mouth

actions.action: counter 'DAY 2'; a small flower opens beside the mound
actions.acting: raven turns his head left and right: still nothing

actions.action: push down to the burrow: a full cobweb with a dew drop, the flower nodding
actions.acting: proof by picture

actions.action: label on the burrow; a small songbird lands on the mound and preens, unafraid
actions.acting: the lightest touch of comedy

actions.action: close: he lets out the breath he has held for two days
actions.acting: shoulders drop, long blink, the first open-beak smile of the film

scenes.summary: Later: three new eggs hatch, the counter climbs back to three, cheeping fills the branches, and far below the jackal passes and gets a wing salute. THE END.

camera.notes: The 'LATER...' card covers 150.4-151.9 (camera cut hidden at its midpoint). Nest close {x 510, y 350, zoom 2.2} to 157.4; then a slow crane out to the whole tree {x 560, y 610, zoom 1.02} by 159.2 and hold for the title.

scenes.composition: Nest close mirrors S2 exactly (same framing, opposite outcome). Final wide: nest and raven upper centre, jackal small at bottom left, cobwebbed burrow and flower bottom right, title across the sky at the top, clear of the nest.

actions.action: transition card 'LATER...'
actions.acting: the tree gains a few more leaves under the card

actions.action: the nest: three new eggs, the raven standing guard beside them
actions.acting: he checks the trunk below once out of habit, then relaxes

actions.action: cracks run across the eggs one, two, three
actions.acting: raven leans in, eyes huge, wings half open

actions.action: three chicks pop up in turn; counter CHICKS 1, 2, 3
actions.acting: stagger 0.35 s; each has its own first look (up, at a sibling, at the father)

actions.action: a small happy jump on the branch
actions.acting: anticipate, hop, landSquash; crest full; wet eyes of the good kind

ending.description: The whole tall tree in frame: three new chicks cheeping in the nest, the raven dipping a wing to the jackal passing below, the burrow closed by a cobweb with a flower beside it. 'THE END' pops in the sky at 159.6 and holds to 163.3 while leaves and chicks keep moving.

new_assets.name: snake
new_assets.description: Black snake whose body follows any path: slither on the ground, spiral up a trunk, coil asleep, rear, strike, lie limp. Pose fields: path (array of points or a function of arc length), out 0..1 (how much has left the hole), wave (phase), rear 0..1, coil 0..1, strike 0..1, limp, tongue 0..1, mouth 0..1, eyes (open | x), plus gaze, lid, alpha.
new_assets.implementation: New Library/cast/snake.js. Sample the path every 6 units; stroke it three times with round caps: black 34 px (outline), near-black #2a2a2a 26 px, then a 4 px yellow belly line offset along the normal; clip red Ben-Day dots (style dot helper) to the lower half. Taper the last 20 % by drawing circles of shrinking radius. Head: a rounded wedge (K path) rotated to the path tangent, one eye2 eye with a yellow iris, optional open jaw (two wedges, red inside), forked tongue as two short lines scaled by tongue. Slither = add a sine offset along the normal with phase from distance travelled. Trunk spiral = alternate path segments drawn before and after the trunk. Wrap in acting() for gaze/lid/sq. The burrow front lip is drawn after the snake so it appears to come out.

new_assets.name: jackal
new_assets.description: The fox figure with a jackal palette: sandy body, grey-black saddle, cream muzzle and chest, black tail tip, ears 10 % taller.
new_assets.implementation: Add an optional pal field to fox (default unchanged, so the regression test stays identical): a small FOXPAL table replacing FOXC and the white tail tip when pal === 'jackal'; the saddle is one extra darker shape clipped to the body. All fox pose fields (sit, plant, raise, reach, ears, tailUp, mouth, talk, brow) then work for the jackal.

new_assets.name: villager
new_assets.description: Parameterised person variants for village people: villageWoman (wife base, headscarf, red dress) and villager (owner base, turban or cap, beard or moustache, tunic colour, width and height factors).
new_assets.implementation: Extend person with an optional costume object {hat:'turban'|'cap'|'scarf'|null, beard, top, bottom, wide, tall}; when absent the three existing kinds draw exactly as now. Hats are 2-3 flat shapes on the head circle. Two new optional pose fields: kneel 0..1 (shorten and fold the legs, lower the hip) and run (walk with amp 1.3 and tip 0.14 is enough; no new code).

new_assets.name: necklace
new_assets.description: Gold bead necklace with a red drop gem that can lie on a surface, hang from a point and swing, and fall.
new_assets.implementation: necklace(ctx, x, y, {hang, ang, open}): 9 yellow circles (r 7, black 3 px outline) on a catenary-like arc from the hang point, rotated by ang from swing(); red teardrop at the bottom; lying state = flat ellipse of beads. Sparkle: four-point star (two crossed diamonds) in white with a black outline, scale and rotation from a pulse.

new_assets.name: bird carry
new_assets.description: Optional bird field carry: a callback or prop name drawn at the beak tip so a held object follows headRot, drop and flight.
new_assets.implementation: If changing bird is not wanted, compute the beak tip in the scene (figure-local offset rotated by headRot, times s and dir) and draw the necklace there after the bird. Either way default drawing is unchanged.

new_assets.name: burrow
new_assets.description: Snake hole in a small rocky mound with states: plain, eyes in the dark, cobweb and flower.
new_assets.implementation: Two functions burrowBack / burrowFront (as pitBack / groundWithPit do): tan mound path with Ben-Day shading, navy oval, three grey rocks; eyes = two yellow ellipses with slit pupils and lid; cobweb = 6 radial white lines + 3 polygon rings with alpha by a 0..1 value; flower = stem line, 5 red petals, yellow centre, scaled up from 0.

new_assets.name: tallTreeHome
new_assets.description: The home set composed from Library sky, hillTrees, ground and tree() with tall custom opts, plus named anchor points (nest fork, low branch, lookout twig, root stone).
new_assets.implementation: bake() once. tree(c, 560, 900, {w: 110, top: 300, crowns: [...6 circles between y 150 and 470...]}); add two branch polygons by hand (nest fork, bare low branch) in trunk brown with the brush outline. Leaves in front of the nest as a second baked layer for depth.

new_assets.name: chaseRoad
new_assets.description: A 3000-unit horizontal strip with four perch trees and the home tree at the end, for the tracking chase.
new_assets.implementation: Bake three 1000-wide tiles of sky + hillTrees + ground and draw tiles by camera x; perch trees are Library tree() calls with small crowns. Camera clamp uses WW = 3000 for this scene.

new_assets.name: fightCloud
new_assets.description: Comic scuffle cloud that hides a fight: churning dust puffs with stars and objects poking out.
new_assets.implementation: fightCloud(ctx, x, y, r, t, seed, pokes): 9-11 paper-white circles with black outline whose centres orbit on K.noise (seeded), red-dot shaded underside, 4 yellow stars popping on a seeded schedule, and poke callbacks (staff tip, tail tip) drawn at the rim. Grows in 4 frames, fades by shrinking the circles.

new_assets.name: dayCycle
new_assets.description: Sky that runs through day, dusk, night and dawn with sun and moon on arcs (name already suggested in the Capabilities Guide).
new_assets.implementation: dayCycle(ctx, p): p 0..1 over one day; draw two sky() presets and cross-fade with globalAlpha; sun() and a moon disc on opposite circular arcs behind the hills; a navy multiply-style overlay (plain alpha rectangle) inside the panel clip for night so the tree and raven read as silhouettes.

new_assets.name: thoughtCloud
new_assets.description: Generic thought cloud large enough to stage action in (name suggested in the Capabilities Guide), used for the peck fantasy and the plan board.
new_assets.implementation: thoughtCloud(ctx, box, t, drawInside): wrap the existing cloud(... inside) helper: scalloped paper outline, three trailing bubbles toward the thinker, clip to the cloud and call drawInside in a local 0..1000 space.

implementation_notes: Film length 163.3 s (MP3 159.304 s + 4.0 s hold). Take every cue from timing.json words; the times in this plan are the word starts from planning/inputs/timeline.md. Word starts can include a little silence, so let actions land 2-3 frames after the cue time, not before it, unless the plan says anticipation.

Screen direction: the burrow and the village-to-home travel are always toward screen right. Villagers enter the home set from the left. The jackal also comes from the left. Keep this in every scene so the geography is never in doubt.

Home set anchors (world units): trunk x 560; nest fork (500, 345); low branch tip (430, 690); lookout twig (600, 215); root stone (395, 862); burrow (860, 890); jackal mark x 200 at s 0.8 (head near (330, 775)). Adjust once in a constants block if the baked tree needs it, and keep S2 and S15 nest framings identical.

Raven: bird {kind:'crow'} at s 1.2 in the home set (s 1.0 on the roof, 0.5 in the plan board). Set LIFE.t = t each frame for blinks; add hand blinks wherever lid is set. Always give him a gaze target.
Both deaths are staged off screen on purpose (S2 whip to the sky; S13 fightCloud). Do not add teeth, blood or a swallowed-chick bulge.
S8 plan board: build it as one function planBoard(ctx, t) with every element on its own pop time; the strip map must stop on the snake appearing (79.7) and must not show the fight.

S11 chase: one position function per runner (kfn on world x) feeding walk() and footfalls(); the raven x is the lead runner x + an offset that shrinks when he waits (110.4) and jumps when he changes tree. Camera x follows the lead runner, so nothing slides.
S14 day cycles are fast (1.4 s and 0.7 s) because the narration gives them only 3.7 s: keep the rest of the frame still so the sky reads.
Sound: only the nine effects listed, all inside the listed pauses, master 0.6. No effect under WHACK, HISS, SWOOP or CHEEP (they fall on spoken words): those are visual only.
Lettering budget: 25 items including labels and counters; none may cover a face. Counters: CHICKS (S2, S15), TREE (S11), DAY (S14) use S.counter in the top left corner.
Use panel-only shake (template) for S13; subtitles never move. Call S.finish last every frame.
After adding the fox pal option, the person costume option and any bird carry field, run node Library/tests/regression.mjs (must report all identical) and rebuild the catalogue.
warnings: The snake is the one large new character (effort L). If time is short, build path, out, wave, rear, limp and tongue first; coil and strike are only needed inside the small thought cloud and can be simple.
Person figures at s 0.45 in the plan board are near the 110 px legibility floor: check a still at phone size; if unreadable, replace them with two bold head-and-body icons.
islandHut, riverBank and figTree positions are taken from the catalogue picture, not measured: confirm the right-bank ground height and the roof ridge point before placing the woman, rock and raven.
The script says "several people ran after him"; the plan uses three (the woman and two men). Add a fourth villager variant only if the chase looks thin.

Carrying the dead snake away on the staff (137.6) is a staging choice to explain why the burrow stays empty; the script only says they killed it. Drop it if the client finds it too dark: leave the limp snake behind the mound instead and remove it under the day cycles.
The LATER card sits over the spoken words "wa ba'da mudda" (150.73-152.5); it is visual only, and subtitles stay readable in the caption panel.
